## Purpose

This SOP describes the general operation, care, and policies governing
the ThermoFisher Delta V Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometer (IRMS) and its
four front-end peripherals in the Oxtoby Environmental Isotope Lab
[@werner2001; @coplen2011]. It is the single instrument-level reference
for all IRMS work. Individual application SOPs (e.g.,
[SOP-L414](SOP-L414-soil-ea-irms.qmd) for soil CN analysis,
[SOP-L415](SOP-L415-carbonate-gasbench-irms.qmd) for carbonate
isotopes) build on this SOP and should be read in conjunction with it.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** The Delta V IRMS and all peripherals (ConFlo IV,
  Flash IRMS EA, TC/EA, GasBench II) in the Oxtoby Isotope Lab,
  SGM Rm 135, Pomona College.
- **Does not apply to:** Application-specific sample preparation, data
  reduction, or QC criteria. See the relevant application SOP.
- **Location:** David W. and Claire B. Oxtoby Environmental Isotope Lab
  (SGM Rm 135). Sample preparation: wet lab (SGM Rm 133).


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                           |
|:------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP; authorize new users                         |
| Lab Manager / Super-User | Certify new users; maintain reactors and gas supply |
| Certified User    | Operate instrument per this SOP; log all sessions       |
| Student Researcher| Operate only under supervision until certified           |


## Definitions

- **ConFlo IV:** Interface hub connecting peripherals, reference gases,
  and the IRMS; handles reference-gas dilution and peak-center
  switching.
- **Delta V IRMS:** The ThermoFisher Delta V Isotope Ratio Mass
  Spectrometer housed in the Oxtoby Isotope Lab, SGM Rm 135.
- **Flash IRMS EA:** Elemental analyzer peripheral that combusts
  samples at 1020 °C to produce N~2~, CO~2~, and (optionally) SO~2~
  for simultaneous $\delta^{15}$N and $\delta^{13}$C analysis.
- **GasBench II:** Low-flow peripheral for headspace gas sampling from
  sealed vials; used for carbonate CO~2~, DIC, and water
  $\delta^{18}$O.
- **H~3~$^{+}$ Factor:** Correction applied to $\delta^{2}$H data for
  H~3~$^{+}$ ions formed in the source that interfere with HD$^{+}$
  at m/z 3.
- **Isodat:** ThermoFisher software used to design analytical
  sequences, control the instrument, and export raw isotope data.
- **Linearity:** The dependence of measured $\delta$ on signal
  amplitude; a well-tuned instrument shows minimal linearity offset
  across the working signal range [@werner2001].
- **Super-User:** Staff or faculty member certified for IRMS operation
  and minor maintenance (gas replacement, reactor exchange).
- **TC/EA:** Thermal Conversion/Elemental Analyzer peripheral;
  pyrolyzes samples at ~1450 °C to produce H~2~ and CO for
  $\delta^{2}$H and $\delta^{18}$O analysis.
- **User:** Student, staff, or faculty member certified to prepare
  samples and operate the IRMS without direct supervision.
- **Zero-Enrichment Test:** Series of reference-gas on/off pulses run
  before analysis to verify the IRMS produces consistent $\delta$
  values independent of signal amplitude [@coplen2011].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Compressed gases:** He, O~2~, CO~2~, N~2~, SO~2~ (where used).
  Cylinders must be chained; O~2~ must be stored away from flammables.
- **High-voltage electronics:** The IRMS source operates at high
  voltage. Do not open the source housing without authorization.
- **High temperatures:** Flash EA reactor operates at 1020 °C; TC/EA
  at ~1450 °C. Allow to cool before maintenance.
- **Chemical:** Tin capsules contain sample material; some samples may
  be hazardous. Handle per the sample-specific SOP.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (during sample loading and reactor maintenance)

### Required Training

- [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
- This SOP (Section on User Certification) before any independent use

## Procedure

### User Certification

Before operating the IRMS independently, personnel must complete the
Training Record (Section 13). Contact the lab manager to schedule
certification.

### Pre-Analysis Checklist

1. Sign in to the lab logbook.
2. Verify He carrier gas pressure (minimum 1500 psi on the regulator).
3. Check reference gas pressures (CO~2~, N~2~ as applicable).
4. Confirm Isodat is running and the instrument status screen shows
   no error flags.
5. Verify the correct peripheral is selected in Isodat.
6. Run a Zero-Enrichment Test (3 on/off pulses) and confirm
   $\delta$ values are stable within ±0.1‰.
7. Run an on/off linearity check if not done within the past 48 h.

### Analytical Sequence Design

1. Open the Isodat Sequence Editor.
2. Load the appropriate method file for the peripheral and analyte.
3. Build the sequence: blank(s), conditioning samples, reference
   materials, unknowns, check standards, blanks.
4. Reference material placement: minimum 1 RM per 10 unknowns;
   two-point normalization requires at least 2 different RMs.
5. Save the sequence file using the naming convention:
   `YYYYMMDD_Project_SeqID_User.seq`

### Starting and Monitoring a Run

1. Load samples into the autosampler or carousel per the
   application SOP.
2. Press **Start** in the Isodat Sequence Editor.
3. Monitor the first 3--5 injections on-screen to confirm peaks are
   present, within expected amplitude, and baseline-resolved.
4. Do not leave the instrument unattended during the first 30 min.

### Shutdown

1. After the sequence completes, export raw data per the application
   SOP.
2. Remove all samples and consumables from the autosampler.
3. Log gas usage and any issues in the lab logbook.
4. Leave the instrument in standby per the lab manager's current
   instructions (the Delta V and ConFlo IV are typically left powered
   on continuously).


## Troubleshooting

| Symptom                              | Possible Cause / Action                       |
|:-------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| High m/z 28 background               | Air leak; check fittings and reactor seals    |
| High m/z 18 background               | Moisture; extend bake-out time                |
| High m/z 40 background               | Air leak (Ar); check fittings                 |
| Poor standard reproducibility        | Capsule sealing; exhausted reactor            |
| No peaks in chromatogram             | Gas flow interrupted; check He supply         |
| Sequence stops mid-run               | Autosampler jam; check carousel alignment     |
| On/off tests fail repeatedly         | Source needs tuning or maintenance            |
| Red/yellow lights on IRMS panel      | Check Isodat error log; contact lab manager   |

If you cannot resolve an issue, **stop the run** and contact the lab
manager. Do not attempt reactor replacement or major maintenance unless
you are a certified Super-User.


## Quality Control

- Run at least two certified reference materials per analytical
  sequence for two-point scale normalization [@paul2007].
- Reference material $\delta$ values must recover within ±0.2‰ of
  certified values; flag sequences that exceed this threshold.
- Blanks (empty tin capsules) must produce no detectable N~2~ or CO~2~
  peak above the noise baseline.
- Archive all raw Isodat sequence files per
  [SOP-L801](SOP-L801-rstudio-github.qmd).

## Training Record

Before using the IRMS independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
3. Read the application SOP for the peripheral(s) they will use
4. Observe at least one complete analysis session by an experienced user
5. Complete supervised practice runs
6. Demonstrate a start-to-finish analysis to the satisfaction of the
   lab technician or a Super-User
7. Be signed off by the lab manager or PI
